"note" doubles as the one-sentence evaluation shown on the page. "recipe" is REAL training hyperparameters extracted directly from each model's checkpoint file (2026-07-12, THE-FINN) -- lora_config+optimizer param_groups for DoRA/LoRA, the full args dict for control-adapters, metadata dict for LatCH heads. NOT hand-written. Re-extract via /tmp .../extract_recipes.py if checkpoints change. Anyone may edit; rebuild + reship after.

adamw_avp_t512_bs1_lr1e4.one_liner: AdamW-vs-FusionOpt A/B: DoRA-r128 on avp, bf16, lr 1e-4, batch 1, T512 (47.6s).
adamw_avp_t512_bs1_lr1e4.why: AdamW and FusionOpt were found to land in nearly-orthogonal weight-space basins (dir cos ~0.1, Fusion moves ~2x farther for the same steps -- CONTINUITY's weight-space read, WORKLOG 2026-07-24) -- so the weight delta alone proves the optimizers are DIFFERENT, not which is BETTER. This sweep answers that with metrics: same DoRA-rows r128 arch/rank/target-modules/corpus as the fp32frames family, only the optimizer (AdamW vs FusionOpt) and precision (bf16 vs fp32) differ, so any metric gap traces to the optimizer/precision choice, not a confound.

adamw_goa_t512_bs1_lr1e4.one_liner: AdamW-vs-FusionOpt A/B: DoRA-r128 on goa, bf16, lr 1e-4, batch 1, T512 (47.6s).
adamw_goa_t512_bs1_lr1e4.why: AdamW and FusionOpt were found to land in nearly-orthogonal weight-space basins (dir cos ~0.1, Fusion moves ~2x farther for the same steps -- CONTINUITY's weight-space read, WORKLOG 2026-07-24) -- so the weight delta alone proves the optimizers are DIFFERENT, not which is BETTER. This sweep answers that with metrics: same DoRA-rows r128 arch/rank/target-modules/corpus as the fp32frames family, only the optimizer (AdamW vs FusionOpt) and precision (bf16 vs fp32) differ, so any metric gap traces to the optimizer/precision choice, not a confound.
